header: Rows that open on click, without a script
lead: Built on native HTML: the browser handles opening, keyboard use and labels for screen readers. Use it for detail that only some readers need.

entries.title: Why details and summary, not a script
entries.bodytext: HTML already has everything an accordion needs: a toggle, a labelled region and keyboard support with Enter and Space. The browser also restores the open state when a reader goes back. Rebuilding this in JavaScript adds a dependency and another way for the element to break.

entries.title: Several rows can be open at once
entries.bodytext: The rows do not share a name, so opening one does not close the others. If only one entry should be open at a time, use the capability tabs instead.

entries.title: All rows print open
entries.bodytext: Otherwise a closed row would print as a heading with no text below it. One print style opens every row, which is the only thing the browser doesn't do by itself.
